prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
This document sets out policy proposals across government.

Public finances and tax
- Raise the personal allowance to at least £13,000; introduce a 30% income tax band between £43,500 and £55,000; lift the 40% threshold to £55,000; increase the transferable allowance for married couples/civil partners; abolish inheritance tax. Use VAT freedoms to zero-rate listed building repairs and sanitary products. Tighten action on multinational tax avoidance. Reduce the cost of government by cutting quangos and ministerial departments where functions can be merged, reducing advisers, and trimming parliamentary costs. Replace the Barnett formula with a needs-based system. Cancel HS2. Lower overseas aid to 0.2% of GNI. Savings fund frontline priorities without higher borrowing.

Immigration and borders
- Leave the EU to end automatic free movement. Introduce a points-based system with an annual cap on highly skilled work visas (around 50,000); a five‑year moratorium on unskilled migration; five visa categories (work, visitor, student, family, asylum); require private health insurance for temporary migrants; five‑year qualifying period for most benefits and routine NHS access; more enforcement against illegal immigration; no amnesty; deport foreign offenders; tackle sham marriages; review family reunion rules.

Health and social care
- Invest an additional £12bn over five years in the NHS. Recruit 8,000 GPs, 20,000 nurses and 3,000 midwives; fund return-to-practice; pilot GPs in A&E; increase mental health and dementia funding; free hospital parking; introduce a statutory “licence to manage” and replace national regulators with locally elected health boards. End new PFI in the NHS; ensure visitors and recent arrivals pay for non-urgent care; seek explicit exclusion of the NHS from international trade deals. Increase social care funding back to 2010 levels over two years; integrate health and social care under the NHS; set a Dignity Code; end 15‑minute care visits; improve carers’ support and pay.

Pensions and welfare
- Introduce a flexible state pension window allowing earlier, actuarially adjusted access; expand funded pensions guidance; criminalise pension cold‑calling; make war widows’ pensions fully lifetime. Replace Work Capability Assessments with GP/specialist assessments; scrap the bedroom tax; protect housing benefit for under‑25s; allow direct rent payments to landlords; tighten benefit rules for recent migrants; limit new child benefit claims to two children; expand foodbank advice services.

Families and childcare
- Retain current free hours and tax‑free childcare but allow vetted informal carers to accept vouchers; expand nursery capacity via planning changes and office conversions; require wrap‑around care (8am–6pm) in primaries; maintain emergency childcare registers. Presume shared parenting on separation; strengthen grandparents’ contact rights; reform family courts; full review of child protection. Restrict mandatory sex education to secondary level with parental transparency.

Education
- Abolish Key Stage 1 SATs; reduce teacher workload; aim to reduce class sizes; end performance‑related pay. Expand academic selection by allowing more grammar places with later transfer options; grow vocational and technical routes; reinstate Intermediate GCSE Maths tier; make first aid part of PSHE. Reverse special school closures. Streamline Ofsted and make inspections more classroom‑focused. In higher education, drop the 50% participation target; waive tuition fee repayment for UK students in approved STEMM degrees who work in the UK for five years; after EU exit, end tuition loans for EEA students.

Housing and planning
- Bring empty homes back into use; prioritise brownfield with a national register, remediation support, and stamp duty relief on first sales; release dormant public land; ease office‑to‑residential conversion. Create a National Homeless Register. Prioritise locals in social housing; restrict access for new arrivals until five years of tax/NI. Protect the green belt; replace the NPPF; enable local referendums on major developments; merge planning and building control. Allow inheritable mortgages; no mansion tax.

Transport
- Cancel HS2; consider additional South East capacity after the airports review; support reopening Manston. Limit speed cameras to safety use; phase out road tolls; oppose pay‑per‑mile tracking; scrap DCPC; adjust the HGV levy to target foreign vehicles post‑EU exit; exempt vehicles over 25 years from VED.

Energy
- Repeal the Climate Change Act; pursue a diverse mix including nuclear, gas, shale, hydro and cost‑effective renewables; end subsidies for new onshore wind and solar PV while honouring existing contracts; support shale with safeguards and a community levy; create a sovereign wealth fund from petroleum taxes; support modern coal with CCS; remove green levies from bills and leave the EU ETS; ban billing penalties on prepay/paper bills.

Employment and small business
- Curb use of EU job portals and relocation grants after EU exit; allow prioritisation of domestic applicants; strengthen minimum wage enforcement. Introduce a zero‑hours code (no exclusivity, 12‑hour notice or pay, right to request secure hours after a year in larger firms). Provide 20% business rates relief up to £50,000 rateable value; penalise systematic late payment by large firms via HMRC; pilot government‑backed trade credit insurance; require 30 minutes’ free town‑centre parking; reduce regulatory burdens; simplify SME access to public contracts.

Farming and fishing
- Replace the CAP with a capped per‑acre payment favouring active farms; premiums for organic and rare breeds; additional hill support; strengthen dairy and sheep supply‑chain fairness; relax burdens on small abattoirs; enhance animal welfare (tougher sentences, lifetime bans, CCTV in abattoirs, regulated religious slaughter, ban live exports). Regain control of UK waters with a 200‑mile EEZ; protect inshore fleets; create no‑take zones; adjust quotas toward under‑10m boats; retain recreational sea angling access.

Heritage, tourism, pubs
- Create a Minister for Heritage and Tourism; zero‑rate VAT on listed building repairs; shift planning presumption to conservation; launch Seaside Town Status with housing and regeneration tools; refocus the Coastal Communities Fund; support pubs via small brewery relief, optional smoking rooms with safeguards, and opposition to minimum alcohol pricing.

Crime, justice and civil liberties
- Add 6,000 frontline posts across police, prisons and borders; invest in technology; review force structures; revise PCC roles; ensure compliant data retention practices. Replace the Human Rights Act with a UK Bill of Rights and make the UK Supreme Court final; end participation in EU justice measures such as the European Arrest Warrant after exit. Tighten laws on grooming, forced marriage, FGM and “honour” crimes; cut fixed‑odds betting terminal stakes to £2. Decriminalise TV licence non‑payment and review the fee. Maintain prison capacity; expand education and restitution; deport foreign offenders swiftly with appeals from abroad.

Political and local reform, culture
- Citizen‑initiated national referendums (2m signatures) every two years; real recall at 20% of constituents; enable open primaries; empower select committees to confirm key appointments and veto specific spending lines. Move to a proportional voting system with a constituency link; restrict general‑election voting to citizens (plus reciprocal cases); replace electoral oversight bodies; end postal voting on demand. Increase local referenda on major planning; keep council tax low; reinstate weekly bins where wanted; act on anti‑social behaviour; curb senior council pay. Promote a common civic culture: official documents in English (and Welsh/Gaelic where appropriate); uphold free speech and a single legal system; mandatory FGM reporting; teach British history chronologically; make St George’s Day and St David’s Day bank holidays.

Trade, defence, overseas aid, EU exit
- Leave the EU via referendum and Article 50; create a Post‑EU Secretariat; seek tariff‑free access to the EU single market and new global trade deals; resume an independent WTO seat; continue cooperation on shared European agencies where beneficial. Raise defence spending to at least 2% of GDP with an extra £4bn by 2020; retain the nuclear deterrent; deliver carrier capability; create a Director of National Intelligence; waive income tax for personnel on overseas operations; oppose an EU army. Reduce overseas aid to 0.2% of GNI over three years (minimum £4bn), close DFID and fold essential functions into the FCO; focus on emergency relief, vaccinations, clean water and sanitation; prioritise trade to drive development.
